narrative.overview: This portfolio treats software work as territory to inspect rather than content to skim. It uses warm drafting paper, marine ink, translucent overlays, and fine construction lines to make a technical practice feel authored rather than templated.
keyCharacteristics: Airy paper-like base instead of dark-interface chrome.
Project entries expand into evidence on hover or keyboard focus.
Fine rules and overlapping imagery create structure without card stacks.
Soft offset shadows appear only on the portrait artifact.

rules.name: The Signal-Not-Theme Rule
rules.body: Coral directs attention; it never becomes a page-wide background or a substitute for hierarchy.

rules.name: The Landmark Rule
rules.body: A large heading should carry the section without a decorative eyebrow competing above it.

rules.name: The Artifact Rule
rules.body: Depth belongs to physical evidence, not every container.

dos: Do lead with real work and let a project title carry visual scale.
Do use fine rules, restrained metadata, and warm negative space to organize information.
Do reserve the colored field fills for active project inspection.
Do retain visible keyboard focus in coral.
donts: Don't return to a dark ground with neon accents.
Don't rebuild the page as a grid of equal cards.
Don't add rounded pills, glass effects, or generic dashboard chrome.
Don't use coral as a substitute for content hierarchy.
